readMe: Every anon-executable, non-trigger SECURITY DEFINER function in `public` must appear in `entries` or `registeredFindings`. The class vocabulary, the finding kinds, and what each means and how it is checked live in tests/helpers/definer-allowlist.mjs (CLASSES, FINDING_KINDS); tests/definer-grants.test.mjs checks each claim against the function's latest body and fails on a missing, stale or doubly-listed name. A body with a comparison against auth.uid() that a NULL uid skips (the NULL-logic guard, nullLogicFlags in tests/helpers/definer-model.mjs) must be fixed, registered as a `gate-skipped-for-anon` finding, or carry `nullLogic: { fingerprint, why }` in its entry, the fingerprint being the body's so an edit re-opens it. scripts/definer-live-diff.mjs applies the same accounting to the live catalog. `fixedAfterCapture` holds what a migration dated after the last live capture fixed (no longer anon-executable in the migrations, or now pinned), with what the list said before (`wasEntry` or `wasFinding` for an anon exposure, `wasPinFinding` for a search_path pin): the capture still shows it open until the owner applies the migration and the catalog is captured again, so the live diff keeps counting it as before and names it as awaiting apply (an unpinned pin fix counts as a registered pin finding meanwhile). Once a capture shows it fixed, delete it.

accept_commitment.note: Flips the caller's own proposed commitment to active (`user_id = auth.uid()`); a signed-out call updates no row.

add_hydration.note: Adds to the caller's own daily snapshot row; raises `not authenticated` when auth.uid() is null.

add_meal_macros.note: Accumulates macros into the caller's own daily snapshot; raises when auth.uid() is null.

award_activity.note: Awards points for the caller's own logged activity (`user_id = v_uid`); returns when auth.uid() is null.

award_checkin_points.note: Awards the caller's own weekly check-in; the ledger row's user is always auth.uid().

award_community_post.note: Awards only for a post the caller authored (`author_id = auth.uid()`).

award_habit.note: Awards only for the caller's own habit completion; the ledger user is auth.uid().

award_meal_log.note: Awards the caller a hard-coded +10 for their own meal log, clamped to their own today; returns when auth.uid() is null.

award_momentum_bonus.note: Awards the caller's own momentum bonus; the amount is computed server-side from the caller's history.

award_my_goal_milestones.note: Reads the caller's own goals and weigh-ins and awards the caller's own milestones.

award_step_points.note: Awards points from the caller's own step snapshots.

award_tier_bonuses.note: Awards the caller's own tier bonuses from their own ledger total.

award_workout_session.note: Awards the caller a hard-coded +10 for their own workout on their own today; amount and category are fixed in the body.

can_access_conversation.note: Boolean: may the CALLER open this conversation (participant, client or owning coach); false for a signed-out caller.

can_access_workout_session.note: Boolean about the caller's own access to a session (its client or its provider's owner).

can_view_community_post.note: Boolean: may the CALLER see this post; public and profile-audience posts read true for anyone, every other audience keys on auth.uid().

channel_unread.note: Unread counts for the caller's own channel memberships only.

check_rate_limit.note: The search rate-limit primitive (2026-08-29), granted to anon by design because the Edge proxy's anon client must reach it: refuses the reserved `self:` namespace, then delegates to _rate_limit_bump, which no client role can execute. A caller can name any other bucket key.

compute_momentum.note: Computes the caller's own momentum score; returns 0 when auth.uid() is null.

consume_ai_proposal.note: Consumes a one-time AI nonce recorded against the caller (`actor_id = auth.uid()`); raises when signed out.

create_channel.note: Creates a channel owned by the caller; raises `Authentication is required` when auth.uid() is null.

dm_unread.note: Unread counts for the caller's own conversation participations only.

get_client_checkins.note: Rows only when is_coach_on_client(p_user_id) holds; anon and non-coaches get an empty set.

get_client_goals.note: Returns null unless is_coach_on_client(p_user_id), and honours the client's `share` opt-out.

get_client_penalties.note: Penalty rows for p_uid only when is_coach_on_client(p_uid) holds.

get_coach_certs.note: Approved certification type and number of a VERIFIED coach for the public coach profile (2026-06-19-coach-certs-public); unverified providers and unapproved rows are filtered in the body.

get_coach_sale_plans.note: A coach's PUBLISHED plans for the storefront; unpublished plans are filtered in the body. Since 2026-10-08-security-review-access-layer.sql the `detail` column comes back without `builder` (the full workout document, unlocked only by get_my_purchased_plans); the preview keys stay (buildType, media, note, the goal/diet/cals meta, the outline `blocks` and a meal plan's `days`, which planPreview.mjs renders before a purchase by design). (as is by_user)

get_coach_sale_plans_by_user.note: The same storefront read keyed by the coach's user id; published plans only, `detail` without `builder` (see get_coach_sale_plans).

get_coach_scores.note: A derived integer score per provider id (at most 200 ids) for public coach cards; exposes no raw counts.

get_coach_waitroom.note: Returns a waiting room only to the coach who owns the provider row (`owner_id = auth.uid()`); anyone else gets `not your waiting room`.

get_follow_stats.note: Accepted follower and following counts of any profile, as shown on public profiles; the caller's own follow flags key on auth.uid() and read false when signed out. Counts are returned for private profiles too.

get_follow_suggestions.note: Suggestions computed from the caller's own follow graph (`auth.uid()`); a signed-out call matches no candidate.

get_market_plans.note: The plan marketplace: published, priced coach plans with the coach display name (limit 60).

get_member_playlists.note: A member's public playlists, shown only when their profile is not private (`shape_profile_visibility`); the caller's own playlists always.

get_my_lift_prs.note: Lift PRs from the caller's own set logs (`client_id = auth.uid()`).

get_my_points_balance.note: Sum of the caller's own score ledger.

get_my_store_credit.note: The caller's own wallet: delegates to get_store_credit_for(auth.uid()), which is service_role only.

get_my_waitlists.note: The caller's own waitlist entries (`client_id = auth.uid()`).

get_or_create_coach_coach_conversation.note: Requires the caller to be a coach on the client (inline subscription and owner check on auth.uid()); raises otherwise.

get_or_create_member_conversation.note: Opens a DM between the caller and another member; raises when auth.uid() is null.

get_public_profile.note: The public profile card: returns what the target's profileVisibility allows this caller to see (a locked card for friends/private). Its migrations grant it to authenticated only, so anon reaches it through the default ACL; the 2026-08-04 migration lists it among the public name/avatar surfaces. Since 2026-10-10 a private profile returns nothing at all to a signed-out caller (the locked card still goes to a signed-in one).

get_radio_song_social.note: Reaction counts and the latest 40 comments (id, author name, body, time) for a radio song key; the caller's own vote keys on auth.uid().

get_roster_weekend_split.note: Restricts the requested client ids to clients the caller coaches (inline subscription join on `owner_id = auth.uid()`); a signed-out call matches none.

invite_from_waitlist.note: Only the coach who owns the provider row may invite (`owner_id = auth.uid()`); anyone else raises.

is_channel_host.note: Boolean about the caller's own host role.

is_channel_member.note: Boolean about the caller's own membership.

is_coach_on_client.note: The authorization primitive itself: true only when auth.uid() owns an active provider row the client is subscribed to; pinned to pg_temp last since 2026-08-02.

is_discipline_coach_on_client.note: The discipline-scoped twin of is_coach_on_client, keyed on auth.uid().

is_public_channel.note: Boolean: is this channel id public. An RLS helper the channel policies call, granted by no migration; it discloses nothing the public channel rows do not.

is_username_available.note: Boolean handle availability, needed by signed-out sign-up and granted to anon on purpose (2026-06-09-usernames.sql); a handle enumeration oracle by design.

list_follow_requests.note: Pending follow requests addressed to the caller (`following_id = auth.uid()`).

nullLogic.why: A language sql body, so there is no reject to write: the comparison is a JOIN filter. `me.user_id = auth.uid()` is an inner join, so a signed-out caller (NULL uid) matches no participant row and the function returns nothing; `other.user_id <> auth.uid()` only narrows rows that survived that join.

log_ai_action.note: Logs against the caller; a target other than the caller requires is_coach_on_client(target). Raises when signed out.

mark_ai_action_undone.note: The action's actor, or a coach on its target (is_coach_on_client), may mark it undone; raises when signed out.

mark_channel_read.note: Updates only the caller's own membership row.

mark_conversation_read.note: Updates only the caller's own participant row.

notify_grocery_list.note: Returns unless is_coach_on_client(p_client) holds; notifies only that client.

post_coach_cosign.note: Requires is_coach_on_client(the post's author) and refuses the caller's own post; raises when signed out.

provider_busy_blocks.note: When a coach is busy, so a booking page shown to signed-out visitors can hide taken times (2026-10-07-booking-rules-time-off.sql): (starts_at, ends_at, kind) only, kind 'time_off' or 'session'; no session id, client, type, status or time-off note. Active sessions only, a window of at most 62 days (longer is refused), nothing that ended more than two days ago, and more than 2000 rows raises rather than returning a cut list. It does disclose a coach's busy pattern by design: that is the information a slot list has to act on.

redeem_store_item.note: Spends the caller's own points; the price comes from store_catalogue server-side; raises `not_authenticated` when signed out.

redeem_store_order.note: As redeem_store_item, for a basket; raises `not_authenticated` when signed out.

release_ai_proposal.note: Deletes only the caller's own nonce (`actor_id = auth.uid()`).

replace_provider_licenses.note: Replaces the caller's own licence rows; raises when signed out.

respond_follow_request.note: Accepts or declines requests addressed to the caller (`following_id = me`); raises when signed out.

revoke_habit.note: Removes the caller's own habit-completion ledger row.

set_channel_pinned.note: Pins a channel for the caller only; raises when signed out.

set_commitment.note: The caller sets their own (active), or a coach on the client (is_coach_on_client) proposes one; anyone else is refused.

set_metric_source.note: The caller's own metric source, or a client's when is_coach_on_client holds; rejects a null auth.uid() first (2026-06-30).

set_my_username.note: Sets the caller's own handle; raises `not_signed_in` when auth.uid() is null.

set_program_detail.note: The client themself, or the coach for that discipline (is_discipline_coach_on_client); rejects a null auth.uid() first (2026-06-30).

toggle_follow.note: Follows or unfollows on behalf of the caller only; raises when signed out.

track_event.note: Analytics events from a fixed name whitelist, DELIBERATELY callable by anon (2026-07-27-session-rpe.sql: it binds auth.uid() itself and rejects unknown names); user_id is NULL when signed out. p_props over 4 KB is stored as {} (2026-10-08), and since 2026-10-10 each caller is capped by _rate_limit_bump in the fn:track_event namespace (120 a minute per cf-connecting-ip when signed out, 60 a minute per auth.uid() when signed in); an event over the cap is dropped, not raised.

waive_penalty.note: Only a coach on the client (is_coach_on_client) may waive; anyone else gets `not_coach`.

fixedAfterCapture.name: get_follow_list
fixedAfterCapture.fix: Signed-in only: EXECUTE revoked from public and anon (authenticated and service_role keep it), and the body now returns rows only for a signed-in caller who is the profile owner, or when the profile is public, or when the caller is an accepted follower (shape_profile_visibility is consulted in the body).

wasFinding.name: get_follow_list
wasFinding.exposed: For ANY user id: id, full name, role and follow date of up to 200 accepted followers or followees, whatever that profile's visibility setting says (public, friends or private). No auth.uid() and no shape_profile_visibility check in the body; granted `to authenticated, anon` by name (2026-06-08-follow-requests.sql:101).
wasFinding.notFixedHere: This change is the audit and its tripwire, and writes no migration. The website profile pages call it too (livingProfilePage.jsx, memberProfile.jsx), and whether signed-out visitors are meant to see follower lists is not something the migrations settle.
wasFinding.ownerCall: Gate it on shape_profile_visibility(p_user_id) (public: anyone; friends or private: the owner or an accepted follower) and decide whether a signed-out visitor may see follower lists at all. Dropping the anon grant is the smaller change.

fixedAfterCapture.name: get_active_now
fixedAfterCapture.fix: Signed-in only: EXECUTE revoked from public and anon (authenticated and service_role keep it). The body is unchanged; the app's Training-now rail reads it signed in, and a signed-out reader gets a permission error the app already treats as an empty rail.

wasFinding.name: get_active_now
wasFinding.exposed: User id, kind (workout or cooking), full name, role, lifetime points, avatar and start time of every member currently mid-workout or cooking (at most 50). No per-member opt-out is consulted, unlike the leaderboard's `leaderboard = off`. Granted `to anon, authenticated` by name (2026-06-09-get-active-now.sql:38).
wasFinding.notFixedHere: It is a documented product surface: the 2026-08-04 migration calls it "granted to anon" and the War Room records the "Training now" presence rail as live with the function "granted anon+authenticated". Removing anon changes the product, which is an owner call and needs a migration this change does not write.
wasFinding.ownerCall: Keep anon access on purpose (then move it to public-by-design with that note), or require sign-in, or add an opt-out the body honours.

fixedAfterCapture.name: shape_profile_visibility
fixedAfterCapture.fix: EXECUTE revoked from public and anon (authenticated and service_role keep it). The body is unchanged; the definers that call it run as their owner, and no RLS policy evaluates it for a signed-out role.

wasFinding.name: shape_profile_visibility
wasFinding.exposed: 'public', 'friends' or 'private' for any user id, and 'public' for an id that does not exist (the body defaults it). A privacy-setting oracle: low sensitivity, but nothing calls it directly from the app or website; it exists for other definers (toggle_follow, get_member_playlists and the PR wall). Granted `to authenticated, anon` by name (2026-06-08-follow-requests.sql:31).
wasFinding.notFixedHere: No migration in this change. Definers call it as their owner, so a client revoke would not break them, but that is an assumption to check against the RLS policies before the grant changes.
wasFinding.ownerCall: Revoke it from public and anon (authenticated kept), after confirming no RLS policy evaluates it for a signed-out role.

fixedAfterCapture.name: get_active_activities
fixedAfterCapture.fix: Signed-in only: EXECUTE revoked from public and anon (authenticated and service_role keep it). The body is unchanged; its one caller returns before the call unless a user is signed in.

wasFinding.name: get_active_activities
wasFinding.exposed: User id, kind and start time of every unexpired activity row, with no cap and no gate. The table's own read policy is `to authenticated` ("any signed-in user, so others can see the dot"), so the definer opens to anon what the table keeps signed-in. Granted `to authenticated, anon` by name (2026-06-09-user-activity.sql:42).
wasFinding.notFixedHere: No migration in this change. The only caller found is the mobile app (shapeBackend.js startActivity), which returns unless a user is signed in.
wasFinding.ownerCall: Revoke it from public and anon and keep authenticated. get_active_now already serves the signed-out rail, if the owner keeps that.

fixedAfterCapture.name: save_workout_session
fixedAfterCapture.fix: alter function public.save_workout_session(jsonb, jsonb, jsonb) set search_path = public, pg_temp; nothing else about it changes.

wasPinFinding.name: save_workout_session
wasPinFinding.why: Declared after the 2026-08-09 sweep with `set search_path = public` and no pg_temp, so the sweep (a snapshot of what existed that day) never touched it and nothing has re-pinned it. The newest migration pins a different function, and that one is a trigger with security invoker.
wasPinFinding.notFixedHere: No migration in this change. It is not anon-reachable (revoked from public and anon, granted to authenticated), so exploiting the gap needs a signed-in caller planting a relation or type in pg_temp.
wasPinFinding.ownerCall: alter function public.save_workout_session(jsonb, jsonb, jsonb) set search_path = public, pg_temp;  (changes nothing else).
